intentAndPurpose.intent: Immediate binary toggle — state takes effect on change without a submit action.

forbids: use in forms requiring explicit submit
replace with Checkbox for non-immediate effects

props.name: accent
props.description: Accent override for selected fill color (code-only; not a Figma component property). When set, overrides the fill from appearance while keeping appearance's border/context. When not set, fill follows appearance role.

props.name: appearance
props.description: Multi-accent appearance role. Interactive checked: explicit role wins; 'auto'/unset resolves to secondary. Interactive unchecked: ignores this prop and uses nearest Surface appearance, then neutral. ReadOnly: neutral in both visual states. Figma API list: auto | neutral | primary | secondary | negative | positive | informative | warning. Extra OneUI roles (`sparkle`, `brand-bg`) remain supported.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible label for switches without a text child.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: ID of an element that labels the switch.

props.name: checked
props.description: Whether the switch is on (controlled). Figma component property: `checked` (matrix chrome may say `selected`).

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Stable anchor for QA / e2e — forwarded to the root switch control only (not the label wrapper).

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the switch is disabled (non-interactive, dimmed). Figma API table mislabels this row as `loading` with a disabled description — the component set has no loading variant; use `disabled`.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.description: Change handler — fires with the next checked value

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Whether the switch is read-only (visually distinct from disabled; remains focusable)

interactionBehavior.summary: The track carries the colour and the knob carries the movement, and the two are kept on separate CSS channels so they never fight: the knob's `translateX` lives on the thumb element while its press-scale lives on the thumb's `::before` pseudo-element. Travel distance is derived live in CSS from `trackWidth − knobSize − 2 × padding` rather than being a standalone token, so it stays correct however the switch is themed or ramped. Two things surprise people. First, the unchecked track ignores the `appearance` prop entirely — it follows the nearest `<Surface>`'s role, and Neutral on the bare page or at the palette extremes — while only the checked track follows `appearance`. Second, although the unchecked track rests on the role's `Moderate` step, hovering jumps it to `Subtle-Hover`, because the system has no hover/pressed token for `Moderate`. `readOnly` is a wholly different look from `disabled`: it stays focusable and repaints as a transparent, outlined track with a smaller ink-coloured dot.
hover: Unchecked, the track fills with `--{Role}-Subtle-Hover`; checked, it fills with `--{Role}-Bold-Hover`.

The unchecked track rests on the role's `Moderate` emphasis but hovers to its `Subtle-Hover` — a different emphasis family. `Moderate` has no hover or pressed token in the system, so the nearest darkened solid surface state is reused.
The knob is deliberately re-pinned on hover: explicit rules re-assert its fill (`--Surface-Default` unchecked, `--{Role}-Bold-TintedA11y` checked) so it can never inherit the track's hover tint.
Every hover rule sits inside `@media (hover: hover)`, so a touch tap leaves no stuck tint behind.
Every hover rule is also qualified `:not([data-readonly])`, so a read-only switch is completely inert under the pointer.
Hover changes the fill only — the track never grows, and the knob does not move.
press: The knob scales UP to `--Switch-thumbPressScale` (1.07 by default). Note the direction: the knob grows, unlike Button which squashes down.

The scale is applied through the `scale` property on the knob's `::before` layer while `translateX` stays on the knob itself, so the press squash and the slide compose cleanly instead of overwriting one another.
The track deepens to `--{Role}-Subtle-Pressed` when unchecked, `--{Role}-Bold-Pressed` when checked.
The track itself never scales — only the knob does.
Press is not `(hover: hover)`-guarded, so touch gets the same feedback; it IS `:not([data-readonly])`-guarded, so a read-only switch gets none of it.
focus: Keyboard focus draws the standard two-layer halo on the track: an inner `--Stroke-XL` gap ring in `--Surface-Halo-Gap` plus an outer ring at `calc(--Stroke-XL + --Focus-Outline-Width)`, so it stays legible inside a tinted `<Surface>`.
The outer ring colour is ALWAYS `--Informative-Bold`, never the appearance role — a `positive` or `negative` switch still focuses informative-blue, per the Figma focus-ring spec.
`:focus-visible` only; `.switch:focus` merely clears the native outline, so a mouse click paints no ring. A global `[data-force-state="focus"]` ancestor hook forces it on for previews.

Unlike hover and press, focus is NOT excluded for `readOnly`: the CSS section comment says read-only has "no hover/focus/pressed states", but the halo selector carries no `:not([data-readonly])` and read-only keeps `tabindex="0"` — so a read-only switch does show the focus ring.
`box-shadow` is in no transition list, so the halo snaps on and off rather than fading.
keyboard: Base UI renders a `<span role="switch">`, not a native `<button>`, and synthesises activation through its button helper: `Enter` activates on keydown and `Space` on keyup, matching native button convention.
Form submission is carried by a hidden `<input type="checkbox">` rendered alongside the span, so `name` still round-trips through a form.
`disabled` sets `aria-disabled="true"` and `tabindex="-1"` — removed from the tab order but still announced. It does NOT use a native `disabled` attribute.
`readOnly` sets `aria-readonly="true"`, does not set `aria-disabled`, and keeps `tabindex="0"` — so it stays reachable by `Tab`, unlike disabled.
The control is wrapped in a `<label>`, so clicking the label text toggles the switch too.
Switch adds no keyboard shortcuts of its own beyond the primitive's activation keys.
selected: Checked fills the track with `--{Role}-Bold` and paints the knob `--{Role}-Bold-TintedA11y`; unchecked fills the track with the surface-resolved `Moderate` and pins the knob to `--Surface-Default` (white).

Which role fills the CHECKED track comes from `appearance` (`auto` or unset resolves to `secondary`). The UNCHECKED track deliberately ignores `appearance` and uses the nearest `<Surface>`'s role, falling back to Neutral on the bare page and at the palette extremes (surface steps 2500 and 100).

The knob's travel is computed in CSS from the live geometry — `trackWidth − knobSize − 2 × padding` — never from a separate `travel` token, so the knob keeps landing exactly at the far padding edge under any theme or size ramp.
Under `[dir="rtl"]` the travel sign flips via `--_sw-inline-sign: -1`, so the knob slides right-to-left.

`accent` (primary / secondary / sparkle) overrides ONLY the checked fill and leaves the appearance role's context colours alone — `appearance="neutral" accent="sparkle"` gives a grey context with a purple fill. `readOnly` drops any accent.
The Figma matrix chrome sometimes labels the boolean `selected`; there is no `selected` prop in React — use `checked` / `defaultChecked`.
disabled: `disabled` dims the whole `<label>` row to `--Disabled-Opacity`, sets `cursor: not-allowed` on that wrapper, and puts `pointer-events: none` on the track.

Here the `not-allowed` cursor IS observable: the track is `pointer-events: none`, so the pointer falls through to the `<label>` wrapper, which declares `not-allowed` and keeps its pointer events. This is unlike a natively `disabled` control (see docs/design/disabled-states.md).

`readOnly` is a different look, not a dim. The wrapper gets `data-readonly` and is explicitly excluded from the opacity rule, the cursor stays `default`, and the track repaints as transparent with a `--Stroke-M` outline in `--Text-High`, padding bumped from `--Spacing-0-5` to `--Spacing-1`, and a knob two f-steps smaller filled with the role's `Bold` ink.

The read-only knob is painted through the thumb's `::before` fill channel, not `background-color` on the thumb — setting the latter is hidden behind the opaque pseudo-element, which is why the dot used to always render white.
`readOnly` also forces both the checked and unchecked state roles to `neutral`.
Figma's API table has a row labelled `loading` that actually describes disabled behaviour; the component set has no loading variant and React exposes no `loading` prop — use `disabled`.
touch: Hover tints never apply on touch-only devices; the pressed track tint plus the knob's +7% growth are the entire tap response.
The track is only `--Spacing-7` / `--Spacing-9` / `--Spacing-10` wide (28 / 36 / 40px) at sizes S / M / L, and its height is just knob + 2 × padding — well under the 44px mobile minimum.
The `<label>` wrapper extends the hit area across the label text, but nothing pads the row to 44px; add your own spacing when you need the mobile touch-target minimum.
